title: HttpClient: typed requests, interceptors and error handling

videos.script:
So far the planner has forgotten everything on reload. Tick a session, reload the page, and the tick is gone, because nothing on the other end kept it. This lesson gives the planner a server to talk to.

{{api}} You write the server first: seventy lines of plain Node, with a data file beside it. The dev server passes it every request that starts with slash A P I.

{{client}} Then HttpClient, Angular's service for requests. The store reads the planner through it, and the screens do not change.

{{typed}} A type argument is a promise, and nothing checks it. One number sent as a string, and the week says eleven thousand minutes. So the store checks the answer where it arrives.

{{writing}} A tick goes to the server now, and survives a reload.

{{interceptors}} An interceptor adds a header to every request, and the server's log shows it arrive.

{{errors}} And you stop the server halfway. The page must not keep saying yes when the server said nothing.
